catalog_quote: As the preceding sections have hinted, accent is an important feature of Tamashek. However, its role is very different in verbs and nouns. For inflected verbs and regularly formed participles, accent is not lexical. Except for the Resit and LoImpfP stems, the accent is assigned by Default Accentuation, hence on the antepenult if there is one, otherwise on the leftmost syllable. ... In the Resit and LoImpfP, however, all verbs undergo ablaut, which includes an accent formative χ-pcl that assigns a marked accent to the first postconsonantal vowel ... For nouns (and other non-verb stems), accent is lexical. Some nouns have a lexical accent, others do not (and so undergo Default Accentuation). A lexical accent is only meaningful when the accent occurs, in the Sg and/or in the PI, in a position where it would not be predictable from Default Accentuation. sweep_summary: Single sweep item: Aikhenvald & Nientao 1988 'On accent in Tamasheq' (Russian, 3 pp., Moscow postgraduate-conference proceedings). Confirmed as a real item from the author's own CV (fetched sources from aikhenvaldlinguistics.com) and the EBALL/Glottolog record, but no digital copy, abstract, DOI, or even a library catalog holding could be located from our machine (Crossref/archive.org/LoC empty; every search engine and library catalog endpoint blocked or rate-limited; Relevance: word accent in a Tuareg variety, but whether it is Mali Tamasheq (taq) or another Tuareg lect is not determinable from the records. It cannot bear on the catalog coding (lexical noun accent + weight-blind antepenult default, from Heath 2005, already confirmed in the held De Gruyter preview) until read; priority medium as a short independent pre-Heath accent statement, not a candidate to supersede Heath. No new first-hand stress statement was read in this sweep; catalog record stands on Heath 2005. Saved:,,,, }.

audit.reasoning: The record rests on the modern 745-page reference grammar by the principal fieldworker (Heath 2005), Glottolog's top grammar for this glottocode, and the deciding quotation, the weight-blindness sentence, the three-syllable-window sentence and the word-vs-phrasal domain evidence are all verbatim in the held legitimate publisher preview at the stated pages (2.10 pp. 20-21, p. 34, p. 41, p. 18, TOC). sources.quote: No word-accent/stress placement rule is given anywhere (all 'stress' hits are either emphasis/syntax or the stative vowel). Only: 'In the stative aspect of the verb, a vowel can be heavily stressed. It is longer than a standard long vowel and heavily accented' and 'The stative differs from the perfective only by the one vowel (or by the stress placed on one vowel)'. This corroborates Heath's grammatical accent formative in the Resultative ('stative') stem but says nothing about default antepenult accent or lexical noun accent.
